      // A resume without an explicit pick must keep serving the agent the
      // conversation was ON (its own model string when one was recorded). The
      // recorded pick wins when there is one (it carries the model half).
      if (dshSessionId !== undefined) {
        this.lockChatAgent(dshSessionId, agentId)
        if (this.chatAgentIntent.has(dshSessionId)) this.syncConversationRoute(dshSessionId)
        else routeBindingRegistry().conversations.set(dshSessionId, resumed.modelId ?? agentId)
      }
      // ...and the persisted pick (model / thought level) is re-applied to the
      // freshly loaded session, whose config comes back at the agent's defaults.
      await this.applyChatChoice(resumed)
      // A RESUMED session had context before this call; a lock written here is
      // not provisional even if the conversation record was missing it.
      resumed.provisionalLock = false
      // The load refreshed the record's mirrors (modes / usage / hasHistory);
      // persist so a later restart restores what this resume saw.
      this.persistAgents()
      return resumed
    }
    // A chat session runs where its DSH session lives, not in the plugin's
    // sandbox directory: the sidebar's workspace selection IS the session's
    // workspace (`sandboxPolicy.resolve` reports it as `workspaceRoot`), and an
    // agent whose cwd is `~/.dsh/dsh-ntr/workspaces` answers "current workspace"
    // with that path while its Read/Glob/Bash cannot see the user's project.
    // That root is trusted on top of the agent's own roots for this session
    // only (see `chatWorkspaceRoot`); the fallback is the configured cwd.
    const workspaceRoot = chatWorkspaceRoot(this.sessionWorkspaceResolver, dshSessionId)
    // What the composer is showing right now. Must be read BEFORE `session/new`:
    // creating the session absorbs its defaults into the catalog, which would
    // overwrite exactly the values the user saw and bring back "displayed one
    // model, ran another". See `displayedChatDefaults`.
    const displayed = dshSessionId === undefined ? undefined : this.displayedChatDefaults(agentId)
    // A1: each chat conversation gets its own process; a call without a DSH id
    // shares the anonymous bucket, exactly like the old `ephemeral:<agent>` key.
    const scope: BridgeScope = dshSessionId === undefined
      ? { kind: 'ephemeral', token: 'anonymous' }
      : { kind: 'chat', dshSessionId }
    const session = await this.bridgeFor(agentId, scope).createSession(
      workspaceRoot ?? cwd,
      workspaceRoot === undefined ? [] : [workspaceRoot],
      // ...and the agent PROCESS runs there too, not just the session: see
      // `ensureReady` for why `session/new`'s cwd alone is not enough.
      workspaceRoot,
    )
    // Absent for `/acp`-RPC sessions and for adapter calls without a chat
    // session; their permission cards are addressed by the ACP session only.
    session.dshSessionId = dshSessionId
    this.dshSessionMap.set(key, session)
    // Turn the displayed defaults into this conversation's pick, so the first
    // prompt runs on what the user was shown (see `seedChatChoiceFromCatalog`).
    if (dshSessionId !== undefined) this.seedChatChoiceFromCatalog(dshSessionId, agentId, session, displayed)
    // Pin what this conversation now runs on, so a route that does not name it
    // (a fresh session replays the deployment default) is rewritten to reality.
    // The recorded pick wins when there is one (it carries the model half);
    // otherwise the agent that just served this turn is pinned bare.
    if (dshSessionId !== undefined) {
      if (this.chatAgentIntent.has(dshSessionId)) this.syncConversationRoute(dshSessionId)
      else routeBindingRegistry().conversations.set(dshSessionId, agentId)
    }
    // Apply whatever the conversation picked BEFORE this session existed — the
    // model and thought level chosen in the composer ahead of the first message.
    // `session/new` answered with the agent's defaults; without this the first
    // turn would run on them and the pick would only take effect afterwards.
    await this.applyChatChoice(session)
    if (dshSessionId !== undefined) {
      // The first ACP session is the moment the conversation's context starts
      // belonging to this agent. The lock is PROVISIONAL until this turn shows
      // something: if it delivers nothing, `rollbackFirstTurn` gives the
      // conversation back (a failed first attempt must not trap it).
      session.provisionalLock = this.lockChatAgent(dshSessionId, agentId)
    }
    // The record is on disk from here: a host restart restores it as parked
    // instead of the next message starting a context-less new session.
    this.persistAgents()
    return session
  }

  /**
   * Take the agent process back from a turn the stall watchdog abandoned.
   *
   * The wedged agent still holds its `session/prompt`, so the next message
   * cannot simply be sent: it would queue behind a turn that may never answer.
   * The process is restarted instead — unless another conversation on the same
   * connection is doing real work, because killing the child destroys THEIR
   * context too, and "retry after they finish" is the honest answer.
   *
   * A restart that can `session/load` costs the conversation nothing: the
   * session is parked `released` and the normal acquisition path resumes it, so
   * chat keeps its lock / `applyChatChoice` semantics and `/acp` keeps
   * `locateOrResume`. An agent without resume support is reset instead, and the
   * user is told the context is gone.
   */
  private async prepareStalledSession(session: LiveSession): Promise<{ ok: true; reset?: boolean } | { ok: false; message: string }> {
    // A session whose `session/close` is still in flight must not be touched:
    // releasing it would park it as resumable and `doResumeSession` flips
    // `closed` back to false, resurrecting a closed session. Its owner deletes
    // the record; the caller's own acquisition creates a new session (chat) or
    // rejects `session_closed` (`/acp`).
    if (session.closed) return { ok: true }
    if (session.released) return { ok: true } // the acquisition resumes it
    const bridge = this.bridgeForSession(session)
    const blocked = `acp: agent "${session.agentId}" is unresponsive, but other conversations are still using it; retry after they finish`
    if (bridge.hasOtherActiveWork(session)) return { ok: false, message: blocked }
    // A sibling conversation the agent already settled is not "work" by
    // `hasOtherActiveWork` — but its HOST may still owe the turn a
    // continuation step (a card it is executing right now), and restarting the
    // process would park and resume that live turn. Its indexed controller is
    // the evidence. Scoped to THIS bridge: the restart kills this bridge's
    // child only, so a sibling conversation on another process (A1) is not a
    // reason to refuse, and a controller of another agent's session never was.
    // A closed or released session has no host behind it (a leftover
    // controller), so it does not pin the child either.
    const owned = this.sessionIdsOf(bridge)
    for (const controller of this.turnStreams.values()) {
      if (controller.session === session) continue
      if (!owned.has(controller.session.sessionId)) continue
      if (controller.session.closed || controller.session.released) continue
      if (!controller.stale) return { ok: false, message: blocked }
    }
    const capabilities = bridge.view().agentCapabilities as { loadSession?: boolean } | undefined
    if (capabilities?.loadSession === true) {
      // Whatever teardown runs, the agent's in-flight `session/prompt` is about
      // to be rejected by the closing connection. Mark the generation so that
      // rejection does not broadcast a second `turn/end` for a turn already
      // finalized by the watchdog (`LiveSession.reclaimedTurnSeq`).
      session.reclaimedTurnSeq = session.turnSeq
      bridge.releaseAll('agent did not acknowledge the stalled turn', 'stalled')
      session.orphanPromptTurnSeq = undefined
      return { ok: true }
    }
    // No resume: the restart IS a reset, so only this session's context is at
    // stake — and any other live session pins the process even while idle.
    if (bridge.sessionList.some(other => other !== session)) return { ok: false, message: blocked }
    const agentId = session.agentId
    // `stop` would ask a wedged agent to close its sessions and wait for an
    // answer that never comes; `forceReset` is the local half only.
    session.reclaimedTurnSeq = session.turnSeq
    bridge.forceReset('agent-stopped')
    this.forgetDshSession(session.sessionId)
    session.orphanPromptTurnSeq = undefined
    this.hub.broadcast({
      type: 'agent/notice',
      agentId,
      level: 'info',
      text: `acp: agent "${agentId}" does not support session resume; the ACP session was reset (context could not be restored)`,
    })
    return { ok: true, reset: true }
  }

  /**
   * 聊天插话的槽位回收：宿主把插话作为同一会话在飞回合的下一步送达，
   * 拒绝会让整条 host turn 失败。ACP 不能向运行中的 prompt 注入消息，
   * 所以按插话语义中止当前回合，等 agent 真正结算后再让调用方重发。
   *
   * 只处理 `claimTurn` 的 `busy`（agent 仍持有本会话 prompt）；`unsettled`
   * 说明我们这一侧已经释放过槽位（用户按过停止），保持原样拒绝。
   *
   * - 控制器已 settle（响应已到，延后收口还没释放闸门）：什么都不取消，只等闸门；
   * - agent 真在跑：走用户取消同一条管线（session/cancel + 结算权限 + cancel fallback），
   *   并立即关闭宿主这一侧的 segment，让闸门在 agent 应答/兜底后打开。
   */
  private async reclaimChatPrompt(
    session: LiveSession,
    controller: TurnStreamController,
    signal?: AbortSignal,
  ): Promise<'ok' | 'aborted'> {
    if (session.closed || session.released) return 'ok'
    if (!controller.hasSettled && session.promptInFlight === true) {
      await this.bridgeForSession(session).cancel(session)
      controller.abortActiveSegment()
    }
    return this.waitForSettleGate(session, signal)
  }

  /** 等 agent 侧 prompt slot 真正释放；步骤被取消时立即返回 aborted。 */
  private waitForSettleGate(session: LiveSession, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<'ok' | 'aborted'> {
    const pending = session.settled
    if (pending === undefined) return Promise.resolve('ok')
    if (signal?.aborted) return Promise.resolve('aborted')
    return new Promise(resolve => {
      const done = (value: 'ok' | 'aborted'): void => {
        signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
        resolve(value)
      }
      const onAbort = (): void => { done('aborted') }
      signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true })
      void pending.then(() => { done('ok') })
    })
  }

  async *streamPrompt(options: GenerateOptions): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
    // The plugin's own conversation↔agent mapping decides who serves the turn
    // (see `bindChatAgent`): the driver may arrive here with the previous
    // agent's id (the logged request header replays) or a session that has
    // never run an ACP turn at all. An explicit binding outranks it.
    //
    // A LOCKED conversation outranks even that: its agent is the one holding
    // the context, so the turn must not be redirected by a stale header, a
    // route registry entry purged by a delete/re-add, or the deployment
    // default. The persisted model half is used when the route no longer names
    // the locked agent.
    const lockedTo = options.sessionId === undefined ? undefined : this.lockedAgentFor(options.sessionId)
    const routed = options.sessionId === undefined ? undefined : this.conversationRouteModel(options.sessionId)
    const model = options.sessionId === undefined
      ? options.model
      : lockedTo !== undefined
        ? (routed !== undefined && splitAdapterModelId(routed).agentId === lockedTo
          ? routed
          : this.chatChoice(options.sessionId)?.modelId ?? lockedTo)
        : routed ?? options.model
    const { agentId, choice } = splitAdapterModelId(model)
    const def = this.defsMap.get(agentId)
    if (def === undefined) {
      yield {
        type: 'finish',
        reason: { kind: 'error', failure: { message: `acp: agent "${agentId}" is not configured`, code: 'unknown_agent' } },
      }
      return
    }

    // Auxiliary host calls (`session-title`, `compaction`) ride the session's
    // logged route, so they reach this adapter looking like a turn. They are not
    // conversation: forwarding one would spend a remote agent turn on a title
    // prompt, or worse, fold it into the ACP agent's own context. Refuse before
    // touching (or spawning) anything — the title service degrades to its text
    // fallback and compaction is best-effort.
    if (options.purpose !== undefined) {
      yield {
        type: 'finish',
        reason: {
          kind: 'error',
          failure: {
            message: `acp: "${options.purpose}" is an auxiliary harness call, not a conversation turn — an ACP agent cannot serve it`,
            code: 'unsupported_purpose',
          },
        },
      }
      return
    }

    // A segmented tool-bearing turn arrives as MANY driver steps. The host
    // loop starts a next step whenever the settled assistant message contains
    // `tool-call` blocks — which is exactly what the ACP agent's cards are —
    // feeding it the staged tool results. Each such step RESUMES the same
    // in-flight `session/prompt` from the transcript cursor: nothing is sent
    // to the ACP agent (it runs its own loop inside ONE prompt call — see
    // `isAcpToolContinuation` and docs/acp-convergence.md §1.7).
    if (isAcpToolContinuation(options.messages ?? [])) {
      const controller = options.sessionId === undefined ? undefined : this.turnStreamFor(options.sessionId)
      if (controller === undefined || controller.stale) {
        // No in-flight turn of ours owns these staged results (a foreign
        // continuation, or one that outlived its turn): answer with one
        // closing message instead of touching the agent.
        const line = `\n[dsh-ntr] this conversation has no in-flight ACP turn to resume; the tool details are in the ACP transcript view.\n`
        yield { type: 'block-start', index: 0, blockType: 'text' }
        yield { type: 'text-delta', index: 0, text: line }
        yield { type: 'block-end', index: 0, block: { type: 'text', text: line } }
        yield { type: 'finish', reason: { kind: 'stop' } }
        return
      }
      const segment = controller.startSegment()
      const onAbort = () => {
        void this.bridgeForSession(controller.session).cancel(controller.session)
        controller.abortActiveSegment()
      }
      if (options.signal?.aborted) onAbort()
      else options.signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true })
      try {
        yield* segment.queue
      } finally {
        options.signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
        // The FINAL continuation step retires the controller: settle ran, this
        // segment closed, and no further continuation can come for its cards.
        if (controller.hasSettled && segment.finished) controller.dispose()
      }
      return
    }

    // Forward the person's own words: the host folds its context sections
    // (AGENTS.md digest, skill catalog, runtime snapshot) after the claimed user
    // batch precisely so a consumer can tell them apart by `source` — see
    const workspaceRoot = chatWorkspaceRoot(this.sessionWorkspaceResolver, options.sessionId)
    const defaultReadFile = (p: string) => {
      try {
        if (existsSync(p)) return readFileSync(p)
        if (workspaceRoot !== undefined && !isAbsolutePath(p)) {
          const joined = join(workspaceRoot, p)
          if (existsSync(joined)) return readFileSync(joined)
        }
      } catch {}
      return undefined
    }

    const resolver = this.attachmentResolver
    const attachmentContext = resolver !== undefined && typeof resolver === 'object' && resolver !== null
      ? Object.assign(Object.create(resolver), {
          readFile: (p: string) => {
            if (typeof (resolver as { readFile?: unknown }).readFile === 'function') {
              try {
                const res = (resolver as { readFile: (p: string) => unknown }).readFile(p)
                if (res !== undefined) return res
              } catch {}
            }
            return defaultReadFile(p)
          },
        })
      : {
          readFile: defaultReadFile,
        }

    const selection = selectForwardPrompt(options.messages ?? [], attachmentContext)
    if (selection.kind === 'no-user-input') {
      // An injected-context wake: nothing the user said, nothing to send.
      yield { type: 'finish', reason: { kind: 'stop' } }
      return
    }
    if (selection.kind === 'empty') {
      yield {
        type: 'finish',
        reason: {
          kind: 'error',
          failure: { message: 'acp: this request carries no user message to forward', code: 'empty_prompt' },
        },
      }
      return
    }

    let session: LiveSession
    // Same key `getOrCreateDshSession` looks up: a session the watchdog left
    // orphaned must be reclaimed BEFORE the acquisition, so this message cannot
    // queue behind a prompt the agent will never answer.
    const stalled = this.dshSessionMap.get(`${options.sessionId ?? 'ephemeral'}:${agentId}`)
    if (stalled !== undefined && stalled.orphanPromptTurnSeq !== undefined) {
      const prepared = await this.prepareStalledSession(stalled)
      if (!prepared.ok) {
        yield {
          type: 'finish',
          reason: { kind: 'error', failure: { message: prepared.message, code: 'agent_unresponsive' } },
        }
        return
      }
    }
    try {
      session = await this.getOrCreateDshSession(options.sessionId, agentId)
    } catch (err) {
      yield {
        type: 'finish',
        reason: { kind: 'error', failure: { message: describeError(err), code: 'session_init_failed' } },
      }
      return
    }

    // The bridge that owns THIS session, not the agent's first slot: an A1
    // agent keeps one process per conversation. Re-resolved through
    // `bridgeForSession` at EVERY use below — a first-turn rollback can close
    // this session and prune its holder (`rollbackFirstTurn` → `pruneBridge`),
    // and a bridge captured once would then `claimTurn` / `beginTurn` /
    // `runPrompt` on a dead object.

    // The model the conversation asks for is not one this agent offers any
    // more: refuse BEFORE sending anything. Falling back to "whatever the agent
    // runs" would silently spend the user's turn on a model they did not
    // choose (different price and capability); the pick is kept so the error
    // and the chip both name the selection that must be replaced.
    const blockedModel = this.staleModelChoice(session, choice)
    if (blockedModel !== undefined) {
      // Nothing was exchanged, so a provisional first turn must hand the
      // conversation back (same rule as any other zero-output failure).
      if (session.provisionalLock === true) this.rollbackFirstTurn(session)
      yield {
        type: 'finish',
        reason: {
          kind: 'error',
          failure: {
            message: `acp: the selected model "${blockedModel}" is not offered by agent "${agentId}" any more; choose another model and send again`,
            code: 'model_unavailable',
          },
        },
      }
      return
    }

    const hasImages = (selection.images?.length ?? 0) > 0 || (selection.content?.some(b => b.type === 'image') ?? false)
    if (hasImages && this.bridgeForSession(session).initResult?.agentCapabilities?.promptCapabilities?.image !== true) {
      if (session.provisionalLock === true) this.rollbackFirstTurn(session)
      yield {
        type: 'finish',
        reason: {
          kind: 'error',
          failure: {
            message: `acp: agent "${agentId}" does not support image input`,
            code: 'image_unsupported',
          },
        },
      }
      return
    }

    // One prompt slot per session, and a turn the user aborted still occupies
    // the AGENT's slot until it acknowledges the cancel (see `claimTurn`).
    let claim = await this.bridgeForSession(session).claimTurn(session)
    if (!claim.ok) {
      // A STEER ("插话"): the host delivers the user's mid-turn message as the
      // NEXT step of the SAME host turn, so the conversation's own ACP prompt
      // is still on air. Refusing would fail the whole host turn. ACP forbids
      // injecting into a running prompt, so the steer's real semantic — abort
      // the current turn, then send this one — is spelled cancel + wait +
      // re-claim here.
      //
      // Only `busy` can be a steer: it means the AGENT still holds OUR prompt
      // (`promptInFlight`). `unsettled` means our side already released the
      // slot (the person pressed stop, or an earlier steer cancelled): the
      // agent has not acknowledged yet, and quietly queueing the next message
      // behind a turn the user stopped is not this path's business — that
      // stays the honest `turn_in_flight` refusal below.
      //
      // Only the conversation's OWN in-flight turn qualifies (its live stream
      // controller, on this very session). A `/acp` RPC turn has no chat
      // controller, and another conversation never reaches this session, so
      // both keep the plain refusal: nothing may be cancelled behind a
      // caller's back.
      const chatController = claim.reason === 'busy' && options.sessionId !== undefined
        ? this.turnStreamFor(options.sessionId)
        : undefined
      if (options.sessionId !== undefined
        && chatController !== undefined
        && !chatController.stale
        && chatController.session === session) {
        const reclaimed = await this.reclaimChatPrompt(session, chatController, options.signal)
        if (reclaimed === 'aborted') {
          // The person pressed stop while the previous turn was winding down:
          // the steer is theirs to re-send, nothing goes to the agent.
          yield {
            type: 'finish',
            reason: { kind: 'aborted', failure: { message: 'aborted', code: 'ABORTED' } },
          }
          return
        }
        // A first turn that produced nothing rolled its provisional lock back
        // and CLOSED (and forgot) this session: the steer needs a fresh one.
        if (session.closed || session.released) {
          try {
            session = await this.getOrCreateDshSession(options.sessionId, agentId)
          } catch (err) {
            yield {
              type: 'finish',
              reason: { kind: 'error', failure: { message: describeError(err), code: 'session_init_failed' } },
            }
            return
          }
        }
        // Re-resolve: the rollback above may have closed the old session AND
        // pruned its holder, and `getOrCreateDshSession` may have built a fresh
        // one under a new bridge.
        claim = await this.bridgeForSession(session).claimTurn(session)
      }
      if (!claim.ok) {
        // Never roll the provisional lock back here: a failed claim means
        // ANOTHER prompt holds the slot (or the agent has not settled it), and
        // that turn owns the conversation's lock. Closing the session would
        // kill a turn that is actively streaming — the refusal already tells
        // the user to retry.
        yield {
          type: 'finish',
          reason: {
            kind: 'error',
            failure: {
              message: claim.reason === 'busy'
                ? 'acp: this session already has a prompt in flight'
                : 'acp: the agent is still finishing the previous (cancelled) turn; send again in a moment',
              code: 'turn_in_flight',
            },
          },
        }
        return
      }
    }

    // Same-agent model/effort switches ride the SAME ACP session (context
    // stays continuous); switching to another agent lands in a separate one
    // via the `${dshSessionId}:${agentId}` key in getOrCreateDshSession.
    // An adapter-DEFAULTED effort is not a choice (see `modelDefaultEffort`):
    // recording or re-applying one would revert the seat's own pick.
    const requestedEffort = options.reasoningEffort
    const turnEffort = requestedEffort !== undefined && requestedEffort === this.modelDefaultEffort(agentId)
      ? undefined
      : requestedEffort
    const aligned = await this.alignSessionConfig(session, choice, turnEffort)
    // The config may have changed between the pre-flight check and this
    // alignment (a `config_option_update` landed in that window). Same rule:
    // never run a model the user did not select.
    if (aligned.modelStale) {
      if (session.provisionalLock === true) this.rollbackFirstTurn(session)
      yield {
        type: 'finish',
        reason: {
          kind: 'error',
          failure: {
            message: `acp: the selected model "${choice ?? ''}" is not offered by agent "${agentId}" any more; choose another model and send again`,
            code: 'model_unavailable',
          },
        },
      }
      return
    }
    // Record what this conversation is now on, so `session/chat-list` can show
    // it without the browser having to derive it from anything else. A
    // materialized-default effort leaves the recorded pick standing: the agent
    // still runs it (the align above was skipped), and erasing it would make
    // the chip claim "default" for a conversation the user explicitly tuned.
    //
    // A BARE route (`agentId`, "let the agent choose") must not overwrite the
    // conversation's own pick: `applyChatChoice` just aligned the session to
    // the value the composer showed (including the defaults seeded for a fresh
    // conversation), and recording the bare id instead sends the model chip
    // back to the agent-level catalog — which any other conversation of the
    // same agent can move.
    const recorded = options.sessionId === undefined ? undefined : this.chatChoice(options.sessionId)
    const recordedModel = recorded !== undefined && recorded.agentId === agentId ? recorded.modelId : undefined
    // No pick at all: report the model the session itself is on (the agent's
    // own default), never the bare route — a bare id would make the chip read
    // the agent-level catalog, which other conversations can move.
    const liveModel = parseCatalogOptions(session.configOptions).model?.currentValue
    const fallbackModel = liveModel !== null && liveModel !== undefined && liveModel !== ''
      ? buildAdapterModelId(agentId, liveModel)
      : model
    const effectiveModel = choice !== undefined ? model : recordedModel ?? fallbackModel
    session.modelId = effectiveModel
    session.choice = choice ?? splitAdapterModelId(effectiveModel).choice
    if (aligned.effortStale) session.reasoningEffort = undefined
    else if (turnEffort !== undefined) session.reasoningEffort = turnEffort

    const promptText = selection.text

    // Re-resolve the ACP-preset verdict every turn (a switch made mid-
    // conversation must land on the next prompt). It is a report for the browser
    // surfaces, not a policy switch: the host arbitrates nothing about the
    // agent's own permissions (see docs/acp-convergence.md §2.3).
    if (session.dshSessionId !== undefined) {
      const resolved = await this.acpModeResolver?.(session.dshSessionId)
      session.acpMode = resolved === true
      // This turn may log an `agent-preset/selected` (a blank-session
      // recompose) and any persistence read observed the log BEFORE it: drop
      // the cached verdict so a later ask re-reads against the moved log.
      this.invalidateAcpMode(session.dshSessionId)
    } else {
      session.acpMode = false
    }

    session.running = true
    session.turnSeq += 1
    const turnGen = session.turnSeq
    session.lastAgentActivityAt = Date.now()
    session.activeToolCalls.clear()
    // A new turn owns the session from here: any reclaim marker named an
    // earlier generation and must not suppress THIS turn's settle.
    session.reclaimedTurnSeq = undefined
    this.armStallTimer()
    const turnId = randomUUID()
    this.hub.broadcast({ type: 'turn/start', sessionId: session.sessionId, turnId, text: promptText })

    // The segmented turn: ONE controller for the whole agent-side prompt, one
    // segment per driver step. The first segment streams until a card-bearing
    // stretch meets the next non-tool event (or the prompt settles); the host
    // loop then executes the card and proposes the continuation step, which
    // resumes the SAME prompt through the branch above.
    const endTurn = this.bridgeForSession(session).beginTurn(session)
    const controller = new TurnStreamController(
      this,
      this.hub,
      session,
      turnId,
      endTurn,
      victim => this.rollbackFirstTurn(victim),
    )
    if (session.dshSessionId !== undefined) this.rememberTurnStream(session.dshSessionId, controller)
    // The session itself carries the controller too: an EPHEMERAL turn
    // (`options.sessionId === undefined`) has no chat id to index under, and
    // the stall watchdog needs SOME route to the controller to close the
    // driver's segment queue. For chat turns this also disambiguates a chat id
    // two LiveSessions briefly share (a concurrent first turn). Assigned AFTER
    // `rememberTurnStream` so the controller it just retired cannot clear this
    // attachment.
    session.turnController = controller
    const segment = controller.startSegment()
    const onAbort = (): void => {
      if (controller.stale) return
      // Re-resolve, but through `bridgeOwning`: an abort must never CREATE
      // a process for a session whose holder was pruned (a rolled-back first
      // turn), and a missing owner means there is nothing left to cancel.
      const owner = this.bridgeOwning(session.agentId, session.sessionId)
      if (owner !== undefined) void owner.cancel(session)
      controller.abortActiveSegment()
    }

    if (options.signal?.aborted) {
      onAbort()
    } else {
      options.signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true })
      // The agent-side turn is in flight from here until its response lands
      // (or the connection dies): that window, not our own stream, is what the
      // next turn has to respect. Settlement reaches the controller, which
      // releases the slot (`endTurn`) whether the segment on air is the first
      // or a continuation one.
      const promptBlocks: ContentBlock[] = selection.content && selection.content.length > 0
        ? selection.content as ContentBlock[]
        : [{ type: 'text', text: promptText }]

      const promptBridge = this.bridgeForSession(session)
      promptBridge.runPrompt(session, promptBlocks, turnId, turnGen)
        .then(result => {
          // The reclaim already ended this turn locally, and the close it
          // performed rejected this very request: the late answer is that same
          // turn, not a second one to broadcast.
          if (session.reclaimedTurnSeq === turnGen) {
            session.reclaimedTurnSeq = undefined
            return
          }
          const responseMeta = codebuddyMetaOf({ _meta: result.meta })
          // A DETACHED-WORKER HOLD: this turn's `Agent` call handed real work
          // to a background worker that has not produced its answer yet, yet
          // the agent answered the prompt normally (CodeBuddy says "已派…" and
          // ends its own turn). Closing here loses the only answer the turn
          // will ever produce — the worker's report streams into this same
          // session later, as a background drain. Hold the turn open until
          // every dispatch reports and the drain goes quiet (see
          // `holdForBackgroundDispatch`); the prompt slot is released there.
          //
          // The decision comes BEFORE `adoptTurnRequestId`: adopting the id
          // would clear the updates the drain streamed while this turn's own id
          // was unknown, and those are exactly the ones the hold must fold.
          const holdDispatch = controller.dispatchedDetachedWorker
            && !session.released
            && !session.closed
            && result.stopReason !== 'cancelled'
          if (!holdDispatch && responseMeta?.conversationRequestId !== undefined) {
            // The response names the conversation turn it queued: an instant
            // answer that still carries one is a real (if silent) turn, and its
            // prose can be told apart from a background drain's.
            controller.adoptTurnRequestId(responseMeta.conversationRequestId)
          }
          // An announced drain that has shown NO sign of life for the staleness
          // window is over, even though nothing said so (CodeBuddy never sends
          // `session_end`). Keeping the record would make a later instant answer
          // with no conversation request id look steered, and hold a normal turn
          // open against a drain that is never coming back. RETIRE the id
          // first, so a late update or a response naming it is never adopted as
          // this session's own turn; then forget the record (the notice de-dupe
          // set with it) so this response settles normally.
          if (session.ambient !== undefined
            && Date.now() - session.ambient.lastActivityAt > this.tuning.ambientStaleMs) {
            retireAmbientId(session, session.ambient.requestId)
            session.ambient = undefined
            session.ambientNotices?.clear()
          }
          if (holdDispatch) {
            // The response may name one run while an announcement named
            // another; the hold accepts both (see `BackgroundHold.acceptedIds`).
            controller.holdForBackgroundDispatch(
              result.stopReason,
              responseMeta?.conversationRequestId ?? responseMeta?.requestId,
            )
            return
          }
          // An instant answer with NO conversation request id, while the agent
          // announced a background drain this turn has not spoken into: the
          // prompt was folded into that drain (CodeBuddy's multitask). The
          // response is a formality — keep the turn open until the drain speaks.
          if (session.ambient !== undefined
            && !session.released
            && !session.closed
            && result.stopReason !== 'cancelled'
            && responseMeta?.conversationRequestId === undefined
            && !controller.hasAgentProse) {
            controller.awaitAmbient(session.ambient.requestId, result.stopReason)
            return
          }
          // No ambient record to wait on, but a drain this session stopped
          // waiting on was retired moments ago: the run may have taken this
          // prompt WITHOUT re-announcing itself. The turn cannot be held open
          // (nothing names the drain), but a silent close must say the output
          // may be in the transcript instead of blaming the agent.
          if (session.ambient === undefined
            && result.stopReason !== 'cancelled'
            && responseMeta?.conversationRequestId === undefined
            && hasRecentRetiredAmbient(session, Math.max(this.tuning.ambientQuietMs * 2, RETIRED_AMBIENT_RECENT_MIN_MS))) {
            controller.noteRecentRetiredDrain()
          }
          controller.settle(result.stopReason === 'cancelled'
            ? { kind: 'cancelled' }
            : { kind: 'stop', stopReason: result.stopReason })
        })
        .catch((err: unknown) => {
          if (session.reclaimedTurnSeq === turnGen) {
            session.reclaimedTurnSeq = undefined
            return
          }
          controller.settle({ kind: 'error', message: describeError(err) })
        })
        // The agent's own answer closed the turn: whatever the watchdog marked
        // orphaned has just reported back and no longer needs a reclaim.
        .finally(() => {
          if (session.reclaimedTurnSeq === turnGen) session.reclaimedTurnSeq = undefined
          this.clearOrphanPrompt(session, turnGen)
          // A rollback during this turn could not prune the holder while the
          // agent was still answering (`hasActiveWork` counts the outstanding
          // prompt). Now that it settled, retry — this is the only second chance
          // a closed-and-forgotten session gets.
          const key = this.keyOfBridge(promptBridge)
          if (key !== undefined) this.pruneBridge(key)
        })
    }

    try {
      yield* segment.queue
    } finally {
      options.signal?.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
      // The FIRST segment never retires its controller here: a card-bearing
      // turn keeps it indexed so its continuation steps can resume the prompt,
      // and a card-less or cancelled one already disposed itself in `settle`.
    }
  }
}

export class AcpLlmAdapter implements LlmAdapterLike {
  constructor(private readonly manager: BridgeManager) {}

  providerInfo(provider: string): LlmProviderInfo {
    return { id: provider, name: 'ACP' }
  }

  providerRetryPolicy(_provider: string): undefined {
    return undefined
  }

  imageRequestPricing(_provider: string, _model: string): undefined {
    return undefined
  }

  /**
   * Advertise NOTHING, on purpose (see `AgentCatalogResult` and
   * `BridgeManager.agentCatalog`).
   *
   * DSH's model catalog is per request, not per session (`buildModelCatalog(ctx)`
   * takes no session id), so an `acp` that listed models would list them in
   * every conversation — including the ones with no ACP agent behind them. The
   * catalog is advisory (its own contract: "an adapter may accept unlisted model
   * ids, and consumers must not turn absence into request rejection"), and route
   * liveness is judged by registration, not by this list, so `acp@agent` and
   * `acp@agent@choice` still resolve and stream while being advertised nowhere.
   * An empty list also keeps this hot path (every `session.models` / `llm.models`
   * request) allocation-free: there is no per-session seam to filter with, so
   * nothing may be listed until there is. The ACP seats read the per-agent view
   * through `agent/catalog` instead.
   */
  async listModels(_provider: string): Promise<readonly LlmModelInfo[]> {
    return []
  }

  async resolveModel(provider: string, model: string, _signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<LlmResolvedModelInfo> {
    return this.manager.resolveAdapterModel(provider, model)
  }

  async prepareCall(provider: string, model: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<PreparedAdapterCall> {
    return {
      model: await this.resolveModel(provider, model, signal),
      stream: (options: GenerateOptions) => this.stream(options),
    }
  }

  stream(options: GenerateOptions): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
    return this.manager.streamPrompt(options)
  }
}

export class AsyncQueue<T> {
  private queue: T[] = []
  private resolvers: Array<(result: IteratorResult<T>) => void> = []
  private closed = false

  push(item: T): void {
    if (this.closed) return
    const resolver = this.resolvers.shift()
    if (resolver) {
      resolver({ done: false, value: item })
    } else {
      this.queue.push(item)
    }
  }

  close(): void {
    if (this.closed) return
    this.closed = true
    while (this.resolvers.length > 0) {
      const resolver = this.resolvers.shift()!
      resolver({ done: true, value: undefined as never })
    }
  }

  async *[Symbol.asyncIterator](): AsyncIterator<T> {
    while (true) {
      if (this.queue.length > 0) {
        yield this.queue.shift()!
      } else if (this.closed) {
        return
      } else {
        const item = await new Promise<IteratorResult<T>>(resolve => {
          this.resolvers.push(resolve)
        })

function describeError(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof Error) {
    const data = (error as { data?: { errorKind?: unknown; message?: unknown } }).data
    const kind = typeof data?.errorKind === 'string' ? data.errorKind : undefined
    const detail = typeof data?.message === 'string' ? data.message : undefined
    const tail = [kind, detail].filter((v): v is string => v !== undefined && v !== '').join(': ')

    resolved.agents,

    resolved.transcriptMaxEntries ?? 600,

      staleCancelMaxRetries: resolved.staleCancelMaxRetries,

}

const AGENT_ID_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/

const NPM_PACKAGE_PATTERN = /^(@[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*\/)?[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*(@[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*)?$/

/**
 * Per-value sanity bound for one `exposedModels` entry. Well above any real
 * model choice value (the longest observed in the wild is 61 chars) but still
 * small enough to refuse a hostile blob.
 */
const EXPOSED_MODEL_VALUE_MAX = 512

/**
 * Total size guard for one `exposedModels` filter.
 *
 * Deliberately a *size* bound and not an entry cap: the number of legitimate
 * values is the agent's own `category: model` choice count, which is unbounded
 * (pi publishes 500 choices, omp 581), so any fixed entry cap is a cap the
 * settings panel can exceed — it would then offer a selection the host refuses
 * with `bad_payload` (the "只显示我选的模型" / "全选" paths send every choice at
 * once). A 1 MiB list is already far beyond any catalog and is the shape a
 * caller would need to abuse the endpoint.
 */
const EXPOSED_MODELS_TOTAL_MAX = 1 << 20

/**
 * Validate and normalize one `exposedModels` filter (order preserved,
 * duplicates dropped).
 *
 * Shared by the persisted-config validator and the `agent/set-exposed-models`
 * RPC route so the two can never drift apart: a filter the panel can build must
 * be accepted by every layer that sees it — including `loadPersistedAgents`,
 * which re-validates the stored config on every boot (a mismatch there silently
 * drops the whole agent definition).
 */
export function normalizeExposedModels(raw: unknown, label: string, code: 'bad_config' | 'bad_payload'): string[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${label} must be an array of model choice values`)
  const seen = new Set<string>()
  const out: string[] = []
  let total = 0
  for (const value of raw) {
    if (typeof value !== 'string' || value === '' || value.length > EXPOSED_MODEL_VALUE_MAX) {
      throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${label} entries must be non-empty strings of at most ${String(EXPOSED_MODEL_VALUE_MAX)} chars`)
    }
    total += value.length
    if (total > EXPOSED_MODELS_TOTAL_MAX) {
      throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${label} is too large (over ${String(EXPOSED_MODELS_TOTAL_MAX)} chars in total)`)
    }
    if (seen.has(value)) continue
    seen.add(value)
    out.push(value)
  }
  return out
}

/**
 * Rebuild the agent tag's halo preference from untrusted input. Only the two
 * enums the settings UI offers are accepted; anything else fails loudly
 * instead of silently switching the tag's look.
 */
export function validateTagHalo(value: unknown): AcpTagHalo {
  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object') throw new AcpError('bad_payload', 'acp: tag halo must be an object')
  const { mode, speed } = value as { mode?: unknown; speed?: unknown }
  if (mode !== 'breath' && mode !== 'steady') throw new AcpError('bad_payload', 'acp: tag halo mode must be "breath" or "steady"')
  if (speed !== 'slow' && speed !== 'normal' && speed !== 'fast') throw new AcpError('bad_payload', 'acp: tag halo speed must be "slow", "normal" or "fast"')
  return { mode, speed }
}

/**
 * Ceiling shared by every approval deadline: one day. Both knobs accept `0`
 * (their meaningful "never" value) and anything up to this, so a range any
 * longer would be a mis-typed number rather than a deliberate window.
 */
export const APPROVAL_DEADLINE_MAX_MS = 86_400_000

/**
 * The shortest REAL wait: the first rung of the card's ladder (30 seconds).
 *
 * The floor for a mode that must not wait zero — see
 * {@link normalizeApprovalWindow}.
 */
export const APPROVAL_DEADLINE_MIN_WAIT_MS = 30_000

/**
 * Make a window legal for the mode it runs under.
 *
 * `0` means 不等待 — the ask is settled the moment it arrives instead of
 * waiting. That is the **auto** mode's business: `auto` answers with the
 * option the agent's own kinds imply, so the agent CONTINUES, and an
 * unattended deployment gets a sane default instead of a hang.
 *
 * Under `abort` the same zero would refuse every ask the instant it arrived:
 * the agent stops at every gate it meets, which is not a timeout, it is a
 * brick wall. So `abort` never offers 不等待, and a window of `0` reaching it
 * (a config file, a state file written by an older build, a mode switch that
 * left the window behind) normalizes to the shortest real wait.
 *
 * `wait` ignores the window entirely — it never expires.
 */
export function normalizeApprovalWindow(mode: PermissionTimeoutMode, ms: number): number {
  return mode === 'abort' && ms === 0 ? APPROVAL_DEADLINE_MIN_WAIT_MS : ms
}

/**
 * The order `auto` mode picks an option in, by the kind the agent declared:
 * the broadest grant first, then the narrow one, then the refusals, then
 * whatever the agent offered instead. See {@link pickAutoOption}.
 */
export const AUTO_OPTION_KIND_PRIORITY = ['allow_always', 'allow_once', 'reject_once', 'reject_always'] as const

/**
 * Validate ONE approval deadline, shared by every layer that accepts one.
 *
 * Three callers, one gate: `validateConfig` (the `cordis.patch.yml` baseline),
 * `validateApprovalDeadlines` (the settings-page write), and
 * `BridgeManager.loadPersistedAgents` (the persisted override, re-validated on
 * every boot because the state file is user-editable). They must agree — a
 * value the panel can save has to survive the next boot, or the setting would
 * silently revert.
 */
export function validateApprovalDeadlineMs(raw: unknown, label: string, code: 'bad_config' | 'bad_payload', hint: string): number {
  if (typeof raw !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(raw) || raw < 0 || raw > APPROVAL_DEADLINE_MAX_MS) {
    throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${label} must be an integer in [0, ${String(APPROVAL_DEADLINE_MAX_MS)}] ${hint}`)
  }
  return raw
}

/**
 * Validate a settings-page deadline write. Omitted keys are simply absent from
 * the result — the manager merges, so a card that only moved the mode must not
 * reset the number. `reset` is not a deadline and is dropped here.
 */
export function validateApprovalDeadlines(value: unknown): Partial<Record<ApprovalDeadlineKey, number>> {
  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object') throw new AcpError('bad_payload', 'acp: approval deadlines must be an object')
  const { permissionTimeoutMs } = value as { permissionTimeoutMs?: unknown }
  const out: Partial<Record<ApprovalDeadlineKey, number>> = {}
  if (permissionTimeoutMs !== undefined) {
    out.permissionTimeoutMs = validateApprovalDeadlineMs(
      permissionTimeoutMs,
      'permissionTimeoutMs',
      'bad_payload',
      '(0 = 不等待，仅自动推进档可用)',
    )
  }
  return out
}

/**
 * Validate the idle-release window the settings page writes.
 *
 * The window is expressed in MILLISECONDS on the shared ladder
 * ({@link IDLE_RELEASE_MS}), so a value the slider can produce is always a
 * value the host runs — the same one-ladder rule the approval deadline card
 * follows.
 */
export function validateIdleReleaseMs(raw: unknown, code: 'bad_config' | 'bad_payload'): number {
  if (typeof raw !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(raw) || !IDLE_RELEASE_MS.includes(raw)) {
    throw new AcpError(code, `acp: idleTimeoutMs must be one of ${IDLE_RELEASE_MS.join(', ')}`)
  }
  return raw
}

/**
 * Validate the mode a write asks for. Three values, and the list is the whole
 * vocabulary: an unanswered ask is either answered for you, kept waiting, or
 * refused. Anything else is a typo, not a new mode.
 */
export function validatePermissionTimeoutMode(raw: unknown, code: 'bad_config' | 'bad_payload'): PermissionTimeoutMode {
  if (raw !== 'abort' && raw !== 'auto' && raw !== 'wait') {
    throw new AcpError(code, 'acp: permissionTimeoutMode must be one of "abort", "auto", "wait"')
  }
  return raw
}

/**
 * The option an expired deadline answers with in `auto` mode.
 *
 * The pick is by the option's KIND, because that is what the agent declared
 * about the choice it is offering: `allow_always` first (one grant covers the
 * rest of the run), then `allow_once` (the smaller grant), then the reject
 * kinds (refuse but let the agent continue), and finally the first option
 * whatever it is — an agent may offer only a custom kind, and refusing to
 * answer at all would hang the turn.
 *
 * `undefined` means NO option could be read (no options, or none with a usable
 * id). The caller then degrades to `abort`: guessing an option is worse than
 * refusing, and hanging is worse than either. OmniTerm dev picks the same way
 * (`pick_auto_option`, `src/acp/permission.rs`).
 */
export function pickAutoOption(options: readonly PermissionOptionView[]): PermissionOptionView | undefined {
  const usable = (option: PermissionOptionView): PermissionOptionView | undefined =>
    option.optionId === '' ? undefined : option
  for (const kind of AUTO_OPTION_KIND_PRIORITY) {
    const hit = options.find(option => option.kind === kind)
    const picked = hit === undefined ? undefined : usable(hit)
    if (picked !== undefined) return picked
  }
  return options.length === 0 ? undefined : usable(options[0] as PermissionOptionView)
}

/**
 * Bound on the number of MCP servers one agent may declare. An MCP server is
 * a process (stdio) or a remote endpoint the agent connects to at session
 * setup, so this list is small in practice; the cap refuses a file-sized list
 * rather than a hostile one.
 */
const MCP_SERVERS_MAX = 32

/**
 * Bound on one MCP server's `name`. The name namespaces the agent's tools as
 * `mcp__<name>__<tool>`, so it has to stay short enough for a tool name.
 */
const MCP_SERVER_NAME_MAX = 64

/**
 * Validate one agent's `mcpServers` list (the plugin's normalized shape, NOT
 * the ACP wire shape).
 *
 * THE ENTRIES ARE RETURNED AS THE USER WROTE THEM — not rebuilt, not
 * defaulted. That is deliberate: the settings panel holds this list as JSON
 * text, and it compares what it would send against what the host stored. A
 * host that reshaped the entries (filling `args: []`, reordering the keys)
 * would make the panel report a change where there is none, and the card
 * would never come clean. So this function VALIDATES and leaves the shape
 * alone; the ACP wire conversion (src/bridge.ts) supplies the defaults the
 * protocol wants.
 *
 * The ACP-transport variant is rejected rather than ignored: it needs the
 * client side of `mcp/message`, which is not in the ACP SDK's stable surface,
 * and no agent advertises `mcpCapabilities.acp`. Accepting it would produce a
 * server the agent can never reach.
 */
export function validateMcpServers(raw: unknown, label: string, code: 'bad_config' | 'bad_payload'): AcpMcpServerDef[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${label} must be an array of MCP servers`)
  if (raw.length > MCP_SERVERS_MAX) {
    throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${label} may hold at most ${String(MCP_SERVERS_MAX)} MCP servers`)
  }
  const seen = new Set<string>()
  const out: AcpMcpServerDef[] = []
  for (const [index, entry] of raw.entries()) {
    const at = `${label}[${String(index)}]`
    if (entry === null || typeof entry !== 'object' || Array.isArray(entry)) {
      throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${at} must be an object`)
    }
    const row = entry as Record<string, unknown>
    const name = row.name
    if (typeof name !== 'string' || name.trim() === '' || name.length > MCP_SERVER_NAME_MAX) {
      throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${at}.name must be a non-empty string of at most ${String(MCP_SERVER_NAME_MAX)} chars`)
    }
    if (seen.has(name)) {
      // The name namespaces the agent's tools (`mcp__<name>__<tool>`), so two
      // servers sharing one would collide inside the agent.
      throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${at}.name "${name}" is used by more than one MCP server`)
    }
    seen.add(name)
    const transport = row.transport
    if (transport === 'acp') {
      throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${at}.transport "acp" is not supported (the agent would have to call back into this plugin over mcp/message)`)
    }
    if (transport === 'stdio') {
      const command = row.command
      if (typeof command !== 'string' || command.trim() === '') {
        throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${at}.command must be a non-empty string for a stdio MCP server`)
      }
      if (row.args !== undefined && (!Array.isArray(row.args) || row.args.some(a => typeof a !== 'string'))) {
        throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${at}.args must be an array of strings`)
      }
      stringMap(row.env, `${at}.env`, code)
      out.push(entry as AcpMcpServerDef)
      continue
    }
    if (transport === 'http' || transport === 'sse') {
      const url = row.url
      if (typeof url !== 'string' || url.trim() === '') {
        throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${at}.url must be a non-empty string for a ${transport} MCP server`)
      }
      stringMap(row.headers, `${at}.headers`, code)
      out.push(entry as AcpMcpServerDef)
      continue
    }
    throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${at}.transport must be "stdio", "http" or "sse"`)
  }
  return out
}

/** One `Record<string,string>` field of an MCP server (env / headers). */
function stringMap(value: unknown, label: string, code: 'bad_config' | 'bad_payload'): void {
  if (value === undefined) return
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) {
    throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${label} must be an object`)
  }
  for (const [key, entry] of Object.entries(value as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    if (typeof entry !== 'string') throw new AcpError(code, `acp: ${label}.${key} must be a string`)
  }
}

// ---- Command lines (`AcpAgentDef.command` is a command LINE, not a bare program) ----

/**
 * Split a command line into tokens, the way a shell would: whitespace
 * separates, single or double quotes group.
 *
 * Inside double quotes a backslash escapes a quote (`\"`) and is otherwise
 * LITERAL — Windows paths are full of backslashes, so treating `\` as a general
 * escape would mangle `"C:\Program Files\agent.exe"`. Best-effort only: an
 * unbalanced quote swallows the rest of the line, which is the same thing a
 * shell does and is reported by the caller as a missing executable.
 */
export function tokenizeCommandLine(raw: string): string[] {
  const tokens: string[] = []
  let current = ''
  let quoted = false
  let touched = false
  let quote: '"' | "'" | undefined
  for (let index = 0; index < raw.length; index += 1) {
    const char = raw[index] as string
    if (quote !== undefined) {
      if (char === '\\' && quote === '"' && raw[index + 1] === '"') {
        current += '"'
        index += 1
        continue
      }
      if (char === quote) {
        quote = undefined
        continue
      }
      current += char
      continue
    }
    if (char === '"' || char === "'") {
      quote = char
      touched = true
      continue
    }
    if (char === ' ' || char === '\t' || char === '\n' || char === '\r') {
      // `touched` keeps an explicitly empty quoted argument (`""`) alive.
      if (touched || current !== '') tokens.push(current)
      current = ''
      touched = false
      continue
    }
    current += char
    touched = true
  }
  if (touched || current !== '') tokens.push(current)
  return tokens
}

/** First token = program, rest = arguments (see {@link tokenizeCommandLine}). */
export function splitCommandLine(raw: string): { command: string; args: string[] } {
  const tokens = tokenizeCommandLine(raw)
  return { command: tokens[0] ?? '', args: tokens.slice(1) }
}

/** Quote one token for a command line — only when it needs it. Inverse of the tokenizer. */
export function quoteCommandToken(token: string): string {
  if (token !== '' && !/[\s"']/.test(token)) return token
  return `"${token.replaceAll('"', '\\"')}"`
}

/**
 * Validate a single agent definition object.
 *
 * `command` is a COMMAND LINE: the whole thing a user would type in a terminal
 * (`codebuddy --acp`) belongs in that one field, and its extra tokens are folded
 * IN FRONT of `args`. Two reasons this is the host's job and not the panel's:
 * `agent/save` / `agent/test` are callable without the panel, and
 * `loadPersistedAgents` re-validates stored defs on every boot.
 *
 * The fold is idempotent ONLY for a whitespace-free command. When the command
 * carries whitespace (a quoted Windows path such as `C:\Program Files\a.exe`),
 * the returned `command` is the BARE path — spawn needs it unquoted
 * (`findExecutable` runs `existsSync` on it, `windowsShimLaunch` re-quotes for
 * cmd.exe; both in src/bridge.ts) — so re-validating that bare command splits it
 * at the space instead of round-tripping. `loadPersistedAgents` closes the gap
 * with `quoteLegacyCommand` (src/bridge.ts): it re-quotes the command token
 * before the re-validate, and only when the path exists on disk. Do not "fix"
 * this by quoting `command` here — that breaks the spawn above.
 */
export function validateAgentDef(entry: unknown, label = 'agent'): AcpAgentDef {
  if (typeof entry !== 'object' || entry === null) throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: ${label} is not an object`)
  const row = entry as Record<string, unknown>
  const id = row.id
  if (typeof id !== 'string' || !AGENT_ID_PATTERN.test(id)) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: ${label}.id must match ${AGENT_ID_PATTERN.source}`)
  }
  if (typeof row.command !== 'string' || row.command.trim() === '') {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" needs a non-empty command`)
  }
  const commandLine = splitCommandLine(row.command)
  if (commandLine.command === '') {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" needs a non-empty command`)
  }
  const extraArgs = row.args ?? []
  if (!Array.isArray(extraArgs) || extraArgs.some(a => typeof a !== 'string')) throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" args must be string[]`)
  const args = [...commandLine.args, ...extraArgs]
  const env: Record<string, string> = {}
  if (row.env !== undefined) {
    if (typeof row.env !== 'object' || row.env === null || Array.isArray(row.env)) throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" env must be an object`)
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(row.env as Record<string, unknown>)) {
      if (typeof v !== 'string') throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" env.${k} must be a string`)
      env[k] = v
    }
  }
  const cwd = row.cwd
  if (cwd !== undefined && (typeof cwd !== 'string' || !isAbsolutePath(cwd))) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" cwd must be an absolute path`)
  }
  const roots = row.allowedCwdRoots ?? (typeof cwd === 'string' ? [cwd] : [])
  if (!Array.isArray(roots) || roots.some(r => typeof r !== 'string' || !isAbsolutePath(r))) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" allowedCwdRoots must be absolute paths`)
  }
  const title = typeof row.title === 'string' && row.title !== '' ? row.title : id
  const npmPackageRaw = row.npmPackage
  if (npmPackageRaw !== undefined && (typeof npmPackageRaw !== 'string' || npmPackageRaw.length > 214)) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" npmPackage must be a string of at most 214 chars`)
  }
  const npmPackage = npmPackageRaw === undefined || (npmPackageRaw as string).trim() === ''
    ? undefined
    : (npmPackageRaw as string).trim()
  if (npmPackage !== undefined && !NPM_PACKAGE_PATTERN.test(npmPackage)) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" npmPackage "${npmPackage}" is not a valid npm package name`)
  }
  const exposedModels = row.exposedModels === undefined
    ? undefined
    : normalizeExposedModels(row.exposedModels, `agent "${id}" exposedModels`, 'bad_config')
  // Optional boolean, ON by default. Only the explicit opt-out is stored:
  // `true` and absent are the same "on" state, so the persisted file does not
  // carry noise.
  const autoDiscoverModels = row.autoDiscoverModels
  if (autoDiscoverModels !== undefined && typeof autoDiscoverModels !== 'boolean') {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" autoDiscoverModels must be a boolean`)
  }
  // Per-agent idle-release window. Kept optional so a stored config from before
  // this field existed still validates (it falls back to the host default).
  const idleTimeoutMs = row.idleTimeoutMs
  if (idleTimeoutMs !== undefined && (typeof idleTimeoutMs !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(idleTimeoutMs)
    || idleTimeoutMs > 86_400_000 || (idleTimeoutMs !== 0 && idleTimeoutMs < 1_000))) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: agent "${id}" idleTimeoutMs must be 0 (never release) or an integer in [1000, 86400000]`)
  }
  // MCP servers the agent should connect to. Optional, so a stored config from
  // before this field existed still validates (the agent then connects only to
  // the servers IT configures for itself).
  const mcpServers = row.mcpServers === undefined
    ? undefined
    : validateMcpServers(row.mcpServers, `agent "${id}" mcpServers`, 'bad_config')
  return {
    id,
    title,
    command: commandLine.command,
    args: args as string[],
    ...(npmPackage !== undefined ? { npmPackage } : {}),
    env,
    cwd: cwd as string | undefined,
    allowedCwdRoots: roots as string[],
    ...(exposedModels !== undefined ? { exposedModels } : {}),
    ...(autoDiscoverModels === false ? { autoDiscoverModels: false } : {}),
    ...(idleTimeoutMs === undefined ? {} : { idleTimeoutMs: idleTimeoutMs as number }),
    ...(mcpServers === undefined ? {} : { mcpServers }),
  }
}

/** Validate the raw plugin config; throws AcpError on any violation (boot fails loudly). */
export function validateConfig(raw: unknown): AcpPluginConfig {
  const value = (raw ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>
  const agentsRaw = value.agents ?? []
  if (!Array.isArray(agentsRaw)) throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: config.agents must be an array')
  const seen = new Set<string>()
  const agents: AcpAgentDef[] = agentsRaw.map((entry, index) => {
    const def = validateAgentDef(entry, `agents[${String(index)}]`)
    if (seen.has(def.id)) throw new AcpError('bad_config', `acp: duplicate agent id "${def.id}"`)
    seen.add(def.id)
    return def
  })
  const max = value.transcriptMaxEntries ?? 600
  if (typeof max !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(max) || max < 50 || max > 100_000) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: transcriptMaxEntries must be an integer in [50, 100000]')
  }
  const probeModelsOnBoot = value.probeModelsOnBoot ?? true
  if (typeof probeModelsOnBoot !== 'boolean') {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: probeModelsOnBoot must be a boolean')
  }
  const startupTimeoutMs = value.startupTimeoutMs ?? 60_000
  if (typeof startupTimeoutMs !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(startupTimeoutMs) || startupTimeoutMs < 1_000 || startupTimeoutMs > 600_000) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: startupTimeoutMs must be a number in [1000, 600000]')
  }
  // ONE wait window for both routes. The two legacy keys are folded in when
  // the new one is absent, so an existing `cordis.patch.yml` keeps meaning what
  // it meant instead of silently falling back to the default.
  const legacyWindow = value.nativeApprovalTimeoutMs ?? value.permissionFallbackTimeoutMs
  // A legacy window of 0 meant "this window never fires". The only way to say
  // that now is the `wait` MODE (0 is 不等待 today), so a legacy zero carries
  // over as the mode — otherwise an unattended deployment would silently turn
  // "wait forever" into "answer immediately".
  const legacyNever = legacyWindow === 0
  const permissionTimeoutMs = validateApprovalDeadlineMs(
    legacyNever ? 300_000 : (value.permissionTimeoutMs ?? legacyWindow ?? 300_000),
    'permissionTimeoutMs',
    'bad_config',
    '(0 = 不等待，仅自动推进档可用)',
  )
  // What an expired deadline DOES. Same validator as the settings-page write,
  // so a mode the panel can offer is a mode the next boot accepts.
  const permissionTimeoutMode = legacyNever
    ? 'wait'
    : validatePermissionTimeoutMode(value.permissionTimeoutMode ?? 'wait', 'bad_config')
  // 不等待 belongs to `auto` (it answers, so the agent continues). Under
  // `abort` a zero window would refuse every ask on arrival — the agent stops
  // at every gate — so it becomes the shortest real wait.
  const effectivePermissionTimeoutMs = normalizeApprovalWindow(permissionTimeoutMode, permissionTimeoutMs)
  // The chat-process idle-release window (the settings page edits it).
  // Same shape as the per-agent field: 0 = never release, otherwise an
  // integer number of milliseconds.
  const idleTimeoutMs = value.idleTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS
  if (typeof idleTimeoutMs !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(idleTimeoutMs)
    || idleTimeoutMs > 86_400_000 || (idleTimeoutMs !== 0 && idleTimeoutMs < 1_000)) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: idleTimeoutMs must be 0 (never release) or an integer in [1000, 86400000]')
  }
  const cancelFallbackMs = value.cancelFallbackMs ?? 15_000
  if (typeof cancelFallbackMs !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(cancelFallbackMs) || cancelFallbackMs < 0 || cancelFallbackMs > 600_000) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: cancelFallbackMs must be an integer in [0, 600000] (0 = disable the fallback)')
  }
  const staleCancelRetryDelayMs = value.staleCancelRetryDelayMs ?? 600
  if (typeof staleCancelRetryDelayMs !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(staleCancelRetryDelayMs) || staleCancelRetryDelayMs < 0 || staleCancelRetryDelayMs > 60_000) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: staleCancelRetryDelayMs must be an integer in [0, 60000] (0 = resend immediately)')
  }
  const staleCancelMaxRetries = value.staleCancelMaxRetries ?? 2
  if (typeof staleCancelMaxRetries !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(staleCancelMaxRetries) || staleCancelMaxRetries < 0 || staleCancelMaxRetries > 5) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: staleCancelMaxRetries must be an integer in [0, 5]')
  }
  // Stall-recovery windows (inactivity watchdog). Two lengths on purpose: a
  // silent turn with the floor is a stuck agent, but a turn waiting on a TOOL
  // call is a working agent, and the tool half may take as long as the guard's
  // own tool-output wait. `0` means "off" / "fall back", never "expire now".
  const turnStallMs = value.turnStallMs ?? 600_000
  if (typeof turnStallMs !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(turnStallMs) || turnStallMs < 0 || turnStallMs > 86_400_000) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: turnStallMs must be an integer in [0, 86400000] (0 = disable the watchdog)')
  }
  const turnStallToolMs = value.turnStallToolMs ?? 1_800_000
  if (typeof turnStallToolMs !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(turnStallToolMs) || turnStallToolMs < 0 || turnStallToolMs > 86_400_000) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: turnStallToolMs must be an integer in [0, 86400000] (0 = fall back to turnStallMs)')
  }
  const turnStallTickMs = value.turnStallTickMs ?? 30_000
  if (typeof turnStallTickMs !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(turnStallTickMs) || turnStallTickMs < 1 || turnStallTickMs > 60_000) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_config', 'acp: turnStallTickMs must be an integer in [1, 60000]')
  }
  return {
    agents,
    transcriptMaxEntries: max,
    probeModelsOnBoot,
    startupTimeoutMs,
    permissionTimeoutMs: effectivePermissionTimeoutMs,
    permissionTimeoutMode,
    cancelFallbackMs,
    staleCancelRetryDelayMs,
    staleCancelMaxRetries,
    turnStallMs,
    turnStallToolMs,
    turnStallTickMs,
    idleTimeoutMs,
  }
}

// ---- Workspace guard ----

/**
 * Win32 drive head: `C:\…` or `C:/…`. Extended-length (`\\?\C:\…`) paths are
 * deliberately NOT matched here — see {@link isExtendedLength}.
 */
const WIN32_DRIVE = /^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/

/**
 * Extended-length (`\\?\…`) / verbatim (`//?/…`) head under either separator
 * spelling. {@link segmentize} does not interpret these forms, and the workspace
 * guard refuses them explicitly rather than mis-parsing a containment — so they
 * are not absolute paths this layer accepts either: config validation rejects a
 * cwd written that way instead of storing one that could never resolve.
 */
function isExtendedLength(p: string): boolean {
  return p.startsWith('\\\\?\\') || p.startsWith('//?/')
}

/**
 * Whether `p` is an absolute path on some platform this plugin runs on: POSIX
 * (`/…`), a Windows drive path (`C:\…`, `C:/…`), or a UNC path
 * (`\\host\share…`, `//host/share…`). The extended-length `\\?\…` family is
 * deliberately NOT absolute here — see {@link isExtendedLength}.
 *
 * Style is judged by the string head only, never deeper content: on POSIX both
 * `\` and `C:` are legal filename characters, so a look past the head would
 * misclassify legitimate POSIX paths.
 *
 * This is the host half of the check; the browser's form validation mirrors it
 * as `isAbsolutePathLike` (src/client/acp-ui.tsx) — keep the two in agreement
 * (tests/acp-view.spec.ts asserts equivalence on a shared sample set).
 */
export function isAbsolutePath(p: string): boolean {
  if (isExtendedLength(p)) return false
  return p.startsWith('/') || WIN32_DRIVE.test(p) || p.startsWith('\\\\')
}

/**
 * Whether `p` is written in a Windows style: a drive head (`C:…`), or a UNC head
 * under EITHER separator spelling (`\\host\share`, `//host/share`).
 *
 * The forward-slash spelling counts because {@link foldSeparators} hands every
 * disk-derived UNC path back in that form: judging style by the separator alone
 * would drop the case folding exactly where it is needed, so `\\SRV\share` and
 * `//SRV/share` would stop matching a configured `\\srv\share` ({@link segmentize}
 * already reads `//host/share` as UNC, and this keeps the two in agreement).
 */
function isWin32Style(p: string): boolean {
  return p.startsWith('\\\\') || p.startsWith('//') || /^[A-Za-z]:/.test(p)
}

/**
 * Comparison form of a path: separators folded (`\` → `/`) and case dropped for
 * win32-style paths, POSIX paths kept byte-exact (a `\` or mixed case is a
 * legitimate filename there). Trailing separators dropped.
 */
function compareForm(p: string): string {
  const win32 = isWin32Style(p)
  // A POSIX backslash is a filename character, not a separator: folding it there
  // would let `/work/a\b` pass as a child of `/work/a`.
  const folded = win32 ? p.replaceAll('\\', '/').replace(/\/+$/, '') : p.replace(/\/+$/, '')
  return win32 ? folded.toLowerCase() : folded
}

/** Fold a realpath (or any disk-derived path) into this layer's canonical spelling: `\` → `/` for win32-style paths. */
function foldSeparators(p: string): string {
  return isWin32Style(p) ? p.replaceAll('\\', '/') : p
}

/** One parsed absolute path: its immutable head (`/`, `C:`, `//host/share`) and the segments under it. */
interface SegmentedPath {
  head: string
  /** Whether the head came from a Windows-style path (drive or UNC) — the fold rule for relative tails. */
  win32: boolean
  segments: string[]
}

/**
 * Split an absolute path into head + segments, folding `\` for Windows-style
 * paths. Returns `undefined` for relative input and for forms this layer does
 * not interpret — extended-length `\\?\…` heads (an agent sending one gets an
 * explicit denial rather than a silently mis-parsed containment).
 */
function segmentize(p: string): SegmentedPath | undefined {
  const drive = /^[A-Za-z]:/.exec(p)
  if (drive !== null) {
    return { head: drive[0], win32: true, segments: p.slice(2).replaceAll('\\', '/').split('/').filter(s => s !== '') }
  }
  if (p.startsWith('//') || p.startsWith('\\\\')) {
    if (p.startsWith('\\\\?\\') || p.startsWith('//?/')) return undefined
    const segments = p.slice(2).replaceAll('\\', '/').split('/').filter(s => s !== '')
    // A UNC path needs both the host and the share before anything under it is addressable.
    if (segments.length < 2) return undefined
    return { head: `//${segments[0]}/${segments[1]}`, win32: true, segments: segments.slice(2) }
  }
  if (p.startsWith('/')) {
    return { head: '/', win32: false, segments: p.split('/').filter(s => s !== '') }
  }
  return undefined
}

/** Lexical `.`/`..`/empty-segment collapse; `..` at a root stays at the root (containment judges the result). */
function collapseSegments(segments: string[]): string[] {
  const stack: string[] = []
  for (const seg of segments) {
    if (seg === '.' || seg === '') continue
    if (seg === '..') stack.pop()
    else stack.push(seg)
  }
  return stack
}

/** The deepest probeable root of a parsed path: `/`, `C:/`, or `//host/share/`. */
function rootForm(parsed: SegmentedPath): string {
  return parsed.head === '/' ? '/' : `${parsed.head}/`
}

/** Rebuild an absolute path from a parsed head and segments (empty segments yield the root form). */
function unsegmentize(parsed: SegmentedPath, segments: string[]): string {
  if (segments.length === 0) return rootForm(parsed)
  // The POSIX head is itself the root slash; a drive/UNC head needs the joiner.
  return parsed.head === '/' ? `/${segments.join('/')}` : `${parsed.head}/${segments.join('/')}`
}

/**
 * Pure path join with lexical `..`/`.` collapse (impl.ts cannot import node:path).
 * The base's head is preserved; a relative tail folds `\` into separators only
 * when the base is Windows-style — a POSIX base keeps `\` as a literal
 * filename character.
 */
function joinWithin(base: string, rel: string): string {
  const parsed = segmentize(base)
  if (parsed === undefined) {
    // Defensive: every caller passes a canonical absolute base.
    return `/${collapseSegments(`${base}/${rel}`.split('/')).join('/')}`
  }
  const folded = parsed.win32 ? rel.replaceAll('\\', '/') : rel
  return unsegmentize(parsed, collapseSegments([...parsed.segments, ...folded.split('/')]))
}

/**
 * Resolve the requested session cwd against the agent's allowed roots.
 * @param def - validated agent definition.
 * @param requested - browser-supplied cwd (optional; `''`/undefined → default).
 * @param realpath - platform realpath (injected; throws if the path is unusable).
 * @param extraRoots - roots trusted on top of the agent's own ones, for THIS
 *   session only. The one caller that matters is a chat session, whose cwd is
 *   the workspace the user picked in the DSH sidebar: that directory is never in
 *   the agent's configured allow-list (the plugin's own sandbox dir is), yet it
 *   is the session's declared workspace — the root the fs guard confines reads
 *   and writes to. `/acp`-RPC sessions pass none and keep `allowedCwdRoots` as
 *   a hard cap.
 * @returns the canonical absolute directory to hand to `session/new` (POSIX
 *   spelling on Windows too: `\` folded to `/`).
 */
export function resolveSessionCwd(def: AcpAgentDef, requested: string | undefined, realpath: (p: string) => string, extraRoots: readonly string[] = []): string {
  const candidate = requested === undefined || requested === '' ? def.cwd : requested
  if (candidate === undefined) throw new AcpError('no_cwd', `acp: agent "${def.id}" has no default cwd; pass one`)
  if (!isAbsolutePath(candidate)) throw new AcpError('bad_cwd', 'acp: session cwd must be absolute')
  let canonical: string
  try {
    canonical = foldSeparators(realpath(candidate))
  } catch {
    throw new AcpError('bad_cwd', `acp: cwd does not exist: ${candidate}`)
  }
  const configured = (def.allowedCwdRoots ?? []).length > 0 ? (def.allowedCwdRoots ?? []) : (def.cwd !== undefined ? [def.cwd] : [])
  const roots = [...configured, ...extraRoots.filter(root => typeof root === 'string' && isAbsolutePath(root))]
  if (roots.length === 0) throw new AcpError('no_roots', `acp: agent "${def.id}" has no allowedCwdRoots configured`)
  const inside = roots.some(root => isUnderPath(canonical, safeRealpath(realpath, root)))
  if (!inside) throw new AcpError('cwd_denied', `acp: cwd ${canonical} is outside agent "${def.id}" allowed roots`)
  return canonical
}

function safeRealpath(realpath: (p: string) => string, p: string): string {
  try {
    return realpath(p)
  } catch {
    return p
  }
}

/**
 * Canonicalize a path requested by an ACP agent (fs/read_text_file,
 * fs/write_text_file) against the session workspace — no containment check.
 *
 * Relative paths join under `sessionCwd`; the collapsed path is canonicalized
 * by realpath up to the nearest existing ancestor (collapsing symlinks and any
 * surviving `..`), with the missing tail re-attached lexically — so a fresh
 * write target with not-yet-created parent directories still validates, and a
 * symlink pointing outside the workspace resolves to its real location (where
 * the containment check then judges it).
 *
 * Windows spellings work throughout: an absolute drive/UNC request keeps its
 * own head, a relative request folds `\` when the session cwd is
 * Windows-style, and the result comes back in the folded `/`-separated form.
 */
export function canonicalizeFsPath(sessionCwd: string, requested: string, realpath: (p: string) => string): string {
  if (typeof requested !== 'string' || requested === '') {
    throw new AcpError('bad_path', 'acp: fs path must be a non-empty string')
  }
  if (isExtendedLength(requested)) {
    // Refused before the relative-join branch can swallow it as a filename: a
    // verbatim path is a form this layer cannot judge, not a path under the cwd.
    // Say so — "does not exist" is a lie when the file is right there.
    throw new AcpError('bad_path', `acp: fs path is a form this layer cannot resolve: ${requested}`)
  }
  const collapsed = isAbsolutePath(requested) ? requested : joinWithin(sessionCwd, requested)
  const parsed = segmentize(collapsed)
  if (parsed === undefined) {
    // segmentize returns undefined for a form it does not interpret — chiefly a
    // UNC head missing its share (`\\host`). Not "does not exist": the target may
    // resolve fine; this layer just cannot address it.
    throw new AcpError('bad_path', `acp: fs path is a form this layer cannot resolve: ${requested}`)
  }
  const segments = collapseSegments(parsed.segments)
  let canonical: string | undefined
  let consumed = 0
  for (let i = segments.length; i >= 0; i--) {
    try {
      canonical = realpath(unsegmentize(parsed, segments.slice(0, i)))
      consumed = i
      break
    } catch { /* walk up to the nearest existing ancestor */ }
  }
  if (canonical === undefined) {
    throw new AcpError('bad_path', `acp: fs path does not exist: ${requested}`)
  }
  const base = foldSeparators(canonical).replace(/\/+$/, '')
  const tail = segments.slice(consumed)
  if (tail.length === 0) {
    // The strip above eats the separator that belongs to a bare root (`/` → ``,
    // `C:\` → `C:`): answer the root's own spelling instead of a value that is no
    // longer absolute.
    return base === '' || base === parsed.head ? rootForm(parsed) : base
  }
  return `${base}/${tail.join('/')}`
}

/**
 * {@link canonicalizeFsPath} plus the allowed-root containment check: a path
 * outside the given `roots` throws (`cwd_denied`) and the caller answers the
 * agent's request with that error instead of touching the disk.
 *
 * The containment is UNCONDITIONAL — there is deliberately no access-mode layer
 * here. The one caller (`guardFsPath` in src/bridge.ts) always passes the
 * agent's own `allowedCwdRoots` plus the session cwd as a hard cap; a DSH
 * access mode such as `danger-full-access` never reaches this path and never
 * lifts the cap.
 */
export function resolveFsPath(sessionCwd: string, roots: readonly string[], requested: string, realpath: (p: string) => string): string {
  const full = canonicalizeFsPath(sessionCwd, requested, realpath)
